git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(audit): fsync the rollback truncate so a failed append's rollback is itself durable (PR #509 review finding I1)

AppendMonotonic already truncated a failed write/sync back to the
pre-write length, but Truncate alone does not flush to disk. A crash
between the truncate and the filesystem's own flush could leave the
pre-truncate length on disk after restart -- exactly the line the
function had just reported as never persisted. Now fsyncs again after
the truncate, best-effort, and says so in the error if that second
fsync also fails too, since the caller (DisclaimDelegation and its ten
siblings) treats a returned error as proof nothing new persisted.
EOF
)"

tool_input.new_string:
func captureStdout(t *testing.T, fn func() error) (string, error) {
	t.Helper()

	oldStdout := os.Stdout
	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	os.Stdout = w
	defer func() { os.Stdout = oldStdout }()

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		_, readErr := buf.ReadFrom(r)
		done <- readErr
	}()

	var closeOnce sync.Once
	closeW := func() { closeOnce.Do(func() { _ = w.Close() }) }
	defer closeW()

	fnErr := fn()
	closeW()

	drainErr := <-done
	require.NoError(t, r.Close())
	require.NoError(t, drainErr)

	return buf.String(), fnErr
}
tool_input.old_string:
func captureStdout(t *testing.T, fn func() error) (out string, fnErr error) {
	t.Helper()

	oldStdout := os.Stdout
	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	os.Stdout = w

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		_, readErr := buf.ReadFrom(r)
		done <- readErr
	}()

	defer func() {
		os.Stdout = oldStdout
		closeWriteErr := w.Close()
		drainErr := <-done
		closeReadErr := r.Close()
		out = buf.String()

		if p := recover(); p != nil {
			panic(p)
		}
		require.NoError(t, closeWriteErr)
		require.NoError(t, drainErr)
		require.NoError(t, closeReadErr)
	}()

	fnErr = fn()
	return
}
